consumer: The frontend's 'is the avatar carrying a knife_combat?' possession check, mirroring the engine's own has_item/has_amount possession predicate over the avatar's full carried reach.
scope: The full possession reach the engine's has_amount/visit_items predicate covers: wielded, worn, and inventory items INCLUDING items nested inside containers (e.g. inside a worn backpack), not just top-level stacks.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items iterates u.wielded_items(), u.worn, and u.inv_const_slice() and emits each top-level item's raw fields as an array; it never recurses into container contents and computes no possession predicate, so it is raw S-class enumeration of the wrong scope rather than the engine's C-class possession result.
divergence: A knife_combat stored inside a worn backpack (or any container): the engine possession predicate returns true, but write_carried_items emits only the top-level container item and omits the nested knife, so the frontend reconstructs 'not carrying' -- a false negative.
